record.title: PolyGraph reports plan-buffered CUDA Graph capture for adaptive speculative decoding
record.summary: The PolyGraph preprint proposes one maximum-grid CUDA Graph with GPU-resident updates for changing speculative-decoding shapes. Its abstract reports a single-H800 trace-driven prototype that replaces 64 shape-specific graphs with one, gives warmed P50 latency of 17.7 vs 17.8 ms and cuts graph-build time from 3,915 to 93 ms. The author also reports a P99 benefit that depends on padding waste. This is a bounded synthetic-trace result, not a production serving demonstration; independent reproduction remains open. The arXiv page says the v1 was submitted on 14 August 2026 despite the identifier prefix 2610, an unexplained metadata discrepancy.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv record identifies PolyGraph as arXiv:2610.23861v1 and gives a version-1 submission date of 14 August 2026. The record's 2610 identifier conflicts with that date; no explanation was available in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The author describes a plan-buffer mechanism that captures one maximum-grid CUDA Graph and writes the active shape to GPU memory before replay; the abstract says this reduces shape-specific graphs from 64 to one using a 28-byte update. On a trace-driven single-H800 prototype with Qwen2.5-3B dimensions, the author reports warmed step latency of 17.7 vs 17.8 ms P50 and graph-build time reduced from 3,915 to 93 ms.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The abstract reports that the P99 advantage over a fixed maximum-padding control is negligible at zero padding waste and reaches 18.7% at 100% padding waste.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The abstract limits the evidence to synthetic traces on one GPU and states that the work is not a production serving system; independent reproduction, production integration and cross-model or cross-hardware transfer are not established.

evidence_gaps.description: The full paper, implementation and trace data were not inspected in this activation; the reviewed source was the official abstract and version history.
All measurements are author-reported for one H800 synthetic-trace prototype; no independent reproduction or production serving evidence was reviewed.
The official arXiv page reports a v1 submission date of 14 August 2026 while the identifier prefix is 2610; no authoritative explanation was found.

brief.importance_rationale: If its bounded mechanism generalizes, shape-aware CUDA Graph replay could reduce graph-capture overhead in inference workloads where speculative decoding changes batch size and draft length. The paper reports only a trace-driven prototype on one H800, so broader serving impact remains unestablished.
limitations: Performance claims are author-reported and based on synthetic traces on one H800.
The result is a custom-kernel prototype and does not establish production-serving benefit.
P99 improvements over maximum padding depend on padding waste and are negligible at zero waste.
The paper's reported August 14 submission date conflicts with the 2610 identifier prefix; this remains unexplained.

Its abstract reports a single-H800 trace-driven prototype that replaces 64 shape-specific graphs with one, gives warmed P50 latency of 17.7 vs 17.8 ms and cuts graph-build time from 3,915 to 93 ms. The author also reports a P99 benefit that depends on padding waste. This is a bounded synthetic-trace result, not a production serving demonstration; independent reproduction remains open. The arXiv page says the v1 was submitted on 14 August 2026 despite the identifier prefix 2610, an unexplained metadata discrepancy.

technical.claimed_result: On one H800 with trace-driven Qwen2.5-3B dimensions, the author reports replacing 64 graphs with one, 17.7 vs 17.8 ms warmed P50, graph-build time reduced from 3,915 to 93 ms, and a P99 improvement over MaxPad that grows with padding waste up to 18.7% at 100% waste.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official abstract documents the proposed mechanism and the author's reported measurements; no independent execution was performed.
technical.implementation_status: Research prototype; the author explicitly says it is not a production serving system.
technical.mechanism: Capture one maximum-grid CUDA Graph; before each replay, update the active batch and draft shape in GPU memory, with kernels skipping tiles outside that shape.
technical.regime: Synthetic trace-driven prototype; one NVIDIA H800; Qwen2.5-3B dimensions; adaptive speculative decoding; custom Triton kernels.
technical.reproducibility: The abstract names the model dimensions and controls, but full methods, code and trace artifacts were not inspected and no reproduction was run.
technical.strongest_baseline: Warmed baseline with shape-specific CUDA Graphs for step latency; MaxPad fixed-draft control for isolating padding waste.

brief.title: PolyGraph reports plan-buffered CUDA Graph capture for adaptive speculative decoding
brief.why_it_matters: Adaptive speculative decoding changes workload shape during generation, while CUDA Graph replay expects fixed launch configurations. If independently reproduced beyond the reported synthetic single-GPU setup, a plan-buffer mechanism could lower capture overhead without padding every step to a maximum shape. The abstract shows little P99 benefit when no padding work is wasted, so the gain is workload-dependent.
